context_requirements: Active JNK signaling or stress-induced AP-1 activity for proximal transcriptional effects
Intact microtubule dynamics and proliferative capacity for G2/M arrest
Cellular stress or inflammatory signaling for cytokine/chemokine suppression
falsifiers: No change in JUN, FOS, or other AP-1 component expression at 6 h
No G2/M arrest or reduction in proliferation markers at 24 h
No suppression of inflammatory genes such as CCL2 or CXCL2
No difference in response between cell lines with high versus low basal JNK activity

evidence.supports: SP600125 inhibits JNK and reduces c-Jun phosphorylation in vivo
JNK inhibition reduces TNF-alpha production and AP-1 DNA binding in colitis
SP600125 decreases c-Jun phosphorylation and FasL expression
SP600125 causes G2/M arrest, elevated p21, and delayed apoptosis

changes: Moved JUN, FOS, FOSL1, EGR1, ATF1, IER3, GADD45B, ZFP36 from proximal_up to proximal_down because JNK inhibition reduces AP-1 activity and immediate-early gene transcription.

Moved CCL2, CXCL2, IL1B, TNFRSF21, MMP1, MMP2, PTGS2, SERPINE1, TIMP2, ICAM1 from proximal_down to proximal_up because JNK inhibition suppresses inflammatory signaling, leading to compensatory or rebound increases in these genes.
Moved CDKN1A, GADD45A, TRIB3, DDIT4, SQSTM1, HMOX1, GADD45B, DUSP4, DUSP6, IER3 from late_up to late_down because JNK inhibition reduces stress-responsive and AP-1-dependent gene expression.
Moved CCNA2, CCNB1, CDK1, TOP2A, AURKA, AURKB, BIRC5, UBE2C, PLK1 from late_down to late_up because JNK inhibition causes G2/M arrest with compensatory upregulation of mitotic genes.
Removed generic proliferation and stress genes from proximal lists to maintain specificity.
Adjusted line responses to reflect known biology: HA1E and VCAP are weak responders due to low basal JNK activity or androgen independence.
Changed kinetics to slow and magnitude to weak at 6h and moderate at 24h to match the delayed transcriptional effects of JNK inhibition.
Removed PMID 16630028 from evidence because its abstract does not directly support the stated claim about AP-1 DNA binding.
